subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questionnaire — Nova Financials RFP
messages:
From: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@novafin.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity questionnaire for RFP (initial)

Sean / Marissa,

Thanks for taking the time on Friday. Per our procurement timeline, we need Redwood's dedicated capacity questionnaire filled out and a preliminary sizing recommendation for our three primary workloads by COB next Wednesday. High-level context below:

- Organization: Nova Financials (regulated fintech)
- Workloads: real-time chat (LLM assistant integrated into client portal), nightly batch summarization/long-context indexing, and embedding generation for search/rerank.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II in progress — we will need details on data separation and audit logs.
- Contract considerations: procurement is looking at 12–24 month reserved capacity commitment with quarterly reviews.

Questions we need answered in the questionnaire:
1) Recommended GPU families and per-pool node counts for predictable 99th percentile latency targets (chat: 150–300ms p99, embeddings: throughput-oriented).
2) Throughput targets: guidance on tokens/sec and concurrent request sizing assumptions for each workload.
3) Reservation planning: minimum guaranteed capacity, burst/overflow strategy across regions, and expected cold-start behavior.
4) Costing: three commitment tiers (12mo/24mo/min-reserve variants) and an example blended $/token for the suggested config.

We attached the RFP questionnaire template. Can you fill and return; procurement will circulate internally. Copying procurement for contract/timeframe clarity.

Appreciate a pragmatic recommendation rather than a conservative max — we want an efficient reserved footprint with safe burst.

Regards,
Daniel
Head of Infrastructure — Nova Financials

Attachment: novafin_rfp_dedicated_qs_template.xlsx (attached to original inbound)
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@novafin.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 14:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questionnaire for RFP (initial)

Daniel —

Thanks for the clear brief. We've completed the questionnaire and attached a compact recommendation set (novafin_dedicated_capacity_qs_filled.xlsx) plus a one-page costing estimate (redwood-costing-estimate.pdf). Below are the highlights and assumptions to help procurement and infra quickly parse trade-offs. If you'd like, we can convert these into a short excel with the exact query mix you expect and re-run the cost model.

Quick summary (recommendation by workload):

1) Real-time chat (client portal assistant)
- Target SLO: p95 < 120ms, p99 <= 300ms for median prompt lengths (avg 350 tokens output).
- Recommended GPU pool(s): primary: H100 80GB (for high throughput + long-context models), fallback pool: A100 40GB quantized variant for high concurrency cost-savings.
- Node sizing (initial reserved): 6 H100 nodes + 8 A100 nodes.
  - Rationale: With our serving runtime and continuous batching, 6x H100 provides ~220 concurrent low-latency streams at ~30 tokens/sec individual yield (approx 6.6k tokens/sec aggregate sustained) assuming warm KV cache. A100s provide an economical headroom for heavy concurrent short-turn requests.
- Autoscaling policy suggestion: reserve 6 H100 (min), scale H100 up to 10 for sustained peak, and allow burst to A100 pool up to 16 nodes via overflow routing.

2) Embeddings (search + rerank)
- Target SLO: throughput > 1.5k embedding vectors/sec (batching-friendly), typical vector dim 1536.
- Recommended GPU pool: L4 (or L40) inference-optimized instances for cost-effective FP16/INT8 embeddings, with an A100 pool for large batched offline jobs.
- Node sizing (initial reserved): 4 L4 nodes + 2 A100 for nightly large batches.
- Batch strategy: server-side batching with per-batch parallelism tuned to keep latency < 200ms for online requests.

3) Nightly summarization / long-context indexing
- Requirement: handle hourly ingestion spikes up to 10k documents with average context 16k tokens during nightly window (2–4 hours).
- Recommended GPU pool: H100 nodes with larger VRAM to hold long KV caches; batch-scaling for throughput jobs.
- Node sizing (initial reserved): 8 H100 nodes reserved for a 4-hour nightly window; can be time-scheduled to downscale outside window.

Reservation and routing model (how we manage guaranteed vs burst):
- Minimum guaranteed capacity: the reserved nodes above (6 H100 + 8 A100 + 4 L4 + 2 A100 + 8 H100-night) — we typically express this as two logical pools (low-latency pool and batch/throughput pool) for contracting.
- Burst/overflow: Redwood supports overflow routing to a shared capacity tier in other regions or to an on-demand fleet controlled by your tenancy. We recommend a burst policy that allows 30–50% additional capacity for unpredictable spikes (paid at on-demand rates).
- Cold start behavior: first-token latency depends on KV-cache warmness and model weights on GPU. With our warm-pool strategy, cold-starts are rare; typical cold-start penalty is 2–6s to load a model into an idle GPU if not pinned. We recommend pinning most chat models on reserved H100 nodes to avoid cold starts for your SLOs.

Throughput assumptions and how we estimated cost (examples):
- Chat: 6 H100 reserved → ~6.6k tokens/sec sustained (warm cache); blended per-token cost (12mo commit) estimated at $0.00038/token for the primary workload in our conservative mix. See attached costing PDF for full tier breakdown.
- Embeddings: 4 L4 reserved → ~1.8k vectors/sec with primed batching; blended $/embedding varied with commit, see sheet.
- Nightly: scheduling reserved time-window reduced effective hourly cost by ~35% vs always-on reservation in most scenarios.

Operational controls and safety nets:
- Model pinning & KV cache warmers for latency-critical endpoints.
- Canary rollout and traffic-splitting by route/model; automatic fallback to quantized A100 variants or hosted shared model if reserved pools degraded.
- Audit logs: token-level request traces (no customer text stored when configured) and per-request TTL logs available to your SIEM via our Private deployment connectors.

Next steps we suggest:
1) We will upload the filled questionnaire and costing to the Drive link and send a short 30-min walkthrough with Infra + Procurement this week (propose Wed 13:00 PST / Thu 09:00 EST).
2) If procurement shares an expected request distribution (sample 24-hour QPS + peak hours), we will re-run the cost model and adjust the reserved mix to hit target blended $/token.
3) We can propose contract language for reserved node definitions, regional failover, and burst pricing.

Attachments: novafin_dedicated_capacity_qs_filled.xlsx, redwood-costing-estimate.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to review line-by-line.

—Sean Gallagher
Director, Solution Sales
Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
From: Procurement <procurement@novafin.com>

Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questionnaire for RFP (follow-up clarifications)

Sean / Marissa —

Thanks for the rapid response and the attachments. A few clarifications before we circulate to legal/finance:

1) Can you split the committed capacity pricing into: a) guaranteed minimum (flat monthly fee), b) preemptible/overflow hourly rate, and c) scheduled-time windowed rates (for nightly jobs)? Procurement would like those as separate line items.
2) For the cold-start concern: what SLAs can Redwood commit to for pinned models? Is there a 99.9% availability SLA on a per-pool basis or do we need an enterprise addon?
3) Regarding regional failover: our primary region is us-west-2 with secondary in us-east-1. If a full us-west outage happens, what is expected failover time and are there cross-region reserved capacity guarantees?

Also: Legal asked if we can get a one-page description of audit-log fields and the default retention periods. SOC 2 evidence will be necessary later in the process.

Can you get these items back by Friday COB? We'll include them in our vendor scoring matrix.

Best,
Procurement Team
Nova Financials

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Procurement <procurement@novafin.com>, Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@novafin.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questionnaire for RFP (final clarifications + deliverables)

Procurement team —

Appreciate the specific asks; attached are three focused deliverables: 1) pricing breakout (redwood-costing-estimate.pdf) with line items for guaranteed monthly reservation, overflow/on-demand hourly, and scheduled-window discounts; 2) a one-page audit-log summary and retention options (included within the PDF); and 3) a proposed SLA / exceptions addendum (redwood-msa-sla-exceptions.docx) that lists per-pool availability commitments and remedies. Highlights below: 

Guaranteed vs overflow pricing (high level) — see PDF for numeric examples:
- Guaranteed monthly (example tier A, 12mo): covers reserved nodes as a flat monthly charge and includes a 10% reserved capacity buffer for maintenance.
- Overflow/on-demand: billed hourly at a higher rate; recommended burst cap 30–50% with pre-negotiated upper-bound spend so procurement has control.
- Scheduled-window pricing: nightly reserved time windows priced at ~65% of always-on reserved cost (reflects ability to time-schedule nodes).

SLAs / availability:
- Base platform SLA: 99.5% per-region availability for hosted pools.
- Enterprise reserved pools (with dedicated nodes & monitoring add-on): 99.9% per-pool availability (this is available under Dedicated capacity contracts and is scoped in the SLA appendix).
- Pinned-model guarantee: we recommend pinning chat-critical models on reserved H100 nodes and including the reserved-node SLA to ensure minimal cold starts. Pinned-model cold-starts are covered under the 99.9% pool SLA; unpinned models have no cold-start SLA.

Cross-region failover:
- Design: active-active routing with health-checks and automated DNS failover. Typical failover time to route traffic after detection is ~45–120 seconds depending on DNS TTL and in-flight request draining.
- Cross-region reserved guarantees require mirrored reserved capacity in the secondary region (contracted as failover capacity). We can model a mirrored standby at reduced commit for cost savings — we included a mirrored standby option in the PDF costing.

Audit logs & SOC 2 evidence:
- Audit logs: request_id, route_id, model_id, timestamp, latency_ms, token_count, requester_id (obfuscated on request), and event_type. Logs are exportable to S3/GCS or streamed to your SIEM via connectors.
- Retention: default 90 days; options: 90/365/indefinite (enterprise). SOC 2 artifacts: Redwood will produce SOC 2 report and map controls — we will coordinate with your security team for evidence transfer (we've handled this with other regulated fintechs).

Next operational suggestion: schedule a 30-min technical alignment between Nova infra, Redwood runtime engineering (cc: karthik_iyer) and our solutions team to confirm concurrency profiles and KV cache priming strategy. Proposed times: Fri 09:00 PST or Mon 10:00 PST — please advise.

Deliverables attached: novafin_dedicated_capacity_qs_filled.xlsx, redwood-costing-estimate.pdf, redwood-msa-sla-exceptions.docx

Regards,

—Sean Gallagher
Director, Solution Sales
Redwood Inference
